paite: Huan hiai vaihawmnate, ama ua na ngak dingte ahi uhi.
heading: Sikhate Bawldan / (Diu 15.12-18)
english: “Now these are the ordinances which you shall set before them:

paite: Hebru sikha na leileh, kum guk sung nang nna asem ding a, akum sagihna ah bangmah pe lou in noplen in apawtkhe ding.
english: “If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh he shall go out free without paying anything.

paite: Ama tum a hong lut ahihleh, ama tum mah in apawtkhe ding. Zi nei ahihleh, azi in amah azuikhe ding.
english: If he comes in by himself, he shall go out by himself. If he is married, then his wife shall go out with him.

paite: Apu in zi apiak a, tapate hiam tanute hiam aneihsakleh, azi leh atate apu a ahi ding ua, amah kia in apawtkhe ding.
english: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.

paite: Sikha in teltak a, "Ka pu ka it, ka zi leh ka tate ka it; noplen in ka pawtkhe kei ding," achihleh;
english: But if the servant shall plainly say, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children. I will not go out free;’

paite: apu in vaihawmte kiang ah amah api dia; kongkhak chiang ah hiam kongkhak khuam chiang ah hiam api dia, apu'n vuhna in abil avut pailet ding. Huchi in ama'n apu nna asem tawntung ding hi.
english: then his master shall bring him to God, and shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.

paite: Mi'n sikhanu ding a atanu azuakleh, sikhapate bang in apaikhe kei ding.
english: “If a man sells his daughter to be a female servant, she shall not go out as the male servants do.

paite: Amah khampa, apu alung-kimsak keileh, apa atankiksak ding. Atung ah muanhuai loutak a ahihleh melmak nam kiang a zuak ding in thuneihna anei kei.
english: If she doesn’t please her master, who has married her to himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt deceitfully with her.

paite: Atapa zi dia adeihleh, tanute bang in abawl ding hi.
english: If he marries her to his son, he shall deal with her as a daughter.

paite: Ama'n zi dang aneihthuahleh, a-an nek, apuansilh leh apiak ding a kilawm asukkiam louh ding ahi.
english: If he takes another wife to himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, and her marital rights.

paite: Atung a hiai thumte ahihkeileh, sum-le-pai pe lou in nonlen in apawtkhe ding ahi.
english: If he doesn’t do these three things for her, she may go free without paying any money.

paite: Asihna dia mi vua peuhmah, sihsak ngeingei ding ahi.
heading: Hiamgamna Toh Kisai Dante
english: “One who strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death,

paite: Mi'n thah ding a na buk lou ahih a, Pathian in akhut a amah apiakkhiakleh, ataikhiakna ding mun ka sehsak ding hi.
english: but not if it is unintentional, but God allows it to happen; then I will appoint you a place where he shall flee.

paite: Himahleh mi khatpeuh in tupmawng in a-invengte tung ah gitlouh piltak in asihna ding in gamta taleh, ka maitam a pan amah na lakhe dia, asih ding ahi.
english: If a man schemes and comes presumptuously on his neighbor to kill him, you shall take him from my altar, that he may die.

paite: Kuapeuh apa hiam, anu hiam vomi, sihsak ngeingei ding ahi.
english: “Anyone who attacks his father or his mother shall be surely put to death.

paite: Kuapeuh mihing gu a zuakmi, ahihkeileh akhut ah muhkhiak a ommi, amah sihsak ngeingei ding ahi.
english: “Anyone who kidnaps someone and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.

paite: Kuapeuh anu leh pa hamsiatmi, sihsak ngeingei ding ahi.
english: “Anyone who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.

paite: Mite kisual uhenla, khat in khat suang in deng hiam, akhuttum hiam in tum henla, si lou in, lupna ngak taleh;
english: “If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone, or with his fist, and he doesn’t die, but is confined to bed;

paite: thou nawn in, chiangkhun khun in kholak vakleh, avopa ahul dia; ahun sukbei man ape dia, amah adamsiangsak sipsip ding hi.
english: if he rises again and walks around with his staff, then he who struck him shall be cleared; only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall provide for his healing until he is thoroughly healed.

paite: Mi'n chiang in asikhapa hiam, asikhanu hiam sat henla, akhutlum in si taleh amah gawt ngeingei ding ahi.
english: “If a man strikes his servant or his maid with a rod, and he dies under his hand, the man shall surely be punished.

paite: Himahleh ni khat hiam, ni nih hiam nung a dam a, athohzohleh, gawt louh ding ahi; amah apu neihsa ahih ziak in.
english: Notwithstanding, if his servant gets up after a day or two, he shall not be punished, for the servant is his property.

paite: Mite kisual in, numei gai lai hihna in, anau tolh henla, himahleh siatdetna in zui keileh; numeinu pasal in atung a, achih bangbang a gawt ngeingei ding ahi. Vaihawmte'n abikhiah bang uh aliau ding hi.
english: “If men fight and hurt a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, and yet no harm follows, he shall be surely fined as much as the woman’s husband demands and the judges allow.

paite: Siatna mawngmawng in zui taleh hinna tang a hinna apiak ding ahi.
english: But if any harm follows, then you must take life for life,

paite: Mit tang a mit, ha tang a ha, khut tang a khut, khe tang a khe.
english: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

paite: Mei a hal tang a mei a hal, liam tang a liam, pawn tang a pawn.
english: burning for burning, wound for wound, and bruise for bruise.

paite: Mi'n asikha mit hiam, asikhanu mit hiam suksak in, se taleh amit ziak in noplen in akhah ding ahi.
english: “If a man strikes his servant’s eye, or his maid’s eye, and destroys it, he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.

paite: Asikhapa ha hiam, asikhanu ha hiam sukhe taleh, aha ziak in noplen in akhah ding ahi.
english: If he strikes out his male servant’s tooth, or his female servant’s tooth, he shall let the servant go free for his tooth’s sake.

paite: Bawngtal in pasal hiam, numei hiam, asik ziak in si taleh; huai bawngtal denlup ngeingei ding ahi. Asa nek louh hial ding ahi. Himahleh abawngtal nei pen gawt louh in asuakta ding hi.
heading: Neitute Mohpuak
english: “If a bull gores a man or a woman to death, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its meat shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall not be held responsible.

paite: Himahleh huai bawngtal amalam a, akii a misik hat hi a, aneitu kiang a hilhsa leng hinapi a, ama'n ana khum tuan lou ahihleh, pasal hiam, numei hiam ana siklupleh, huai bawngtal denlup ding ahi a; aneitu leng sihsak ding ahi.
english: But if the bull had a habit of goring in the past, and this has been testified to its owner, and he has not kept it in, but it has killed a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death.

paite: Atung ah dangka sum akiphutleh, akiphut bangbang ahinna tatna man ding in ape ding ahi.
english: If a ransom is imposed on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is imposed.

paite: Tapa hiam, tanu hiam ana sikleh, hiai vaihawmna bang a, atung a hih ding ahi.
english: Whether it has gored a son or has gored a daughter, according to this judgment it shall be done to him.

paite: Bawngtal in sikhapa hiam sikhanu hiam asikleh, apu kiang ah dangka shekel sawmthum ape dia, bawngtal pen denlup ding ahi.
english: If the bull gores a male servant or a female servant, thirty shekels of silver shall be given to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.

paite: Pasal in kokhuk sin hong henla, ahihkeileh pasal in kokhuk tou henla, sin kei henla, asung ah bawngtal hiam sabiltung hiam ke taleh,
english: “If a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and doesn’t cover it, and a bull or a donkey falls into it,

paite: kokhuk neitu in abawlhoih a, aneipa kiang a dangka sum apiak ding ahi. Huchi in aganta si pen amah a ahi ding.
english: the owner of the pit shall make it good. He shall give money to its owner, and the dead animal shall be his.

paite: Mi khat bawngtal in midang khat bawngtal mah hih na kha henla, si taleh; abawngtal hing lai pen azuak ding ua, asum akihawm ding uhi. Abawngtal si pen leng akihawm ding uh ahi.
english: “If one man’s bull injures another’s, so that it dies, then they shall sell the live bull, and divide its price; and they shall also divide the dead animal.

paite: Ahihkeileh amalam a huai bawngtal sik hat ahi chih akitheih a, aneitu in akhum kei chih akitheihleh; bawngtal tang a bawngtal apiak ngeingei ding ahi. Huchi in aganta si pen amah a tuam ahi ding hi.
english: Or if it is known that the bull was in the habit of goring in the past, and its owner has not kept it in, he shall surely pay bull for bull, and the dead animal shall be his own.
